content.text: A long-term advantage, measured four weeks after feedback provision, was evident only for direct corrections (Bonilla López et al., 2018). Notably, learners reported significantly lower cognitive load when revising after direct corrections on grammatical errors than after metalinguistic codes on grammatical and non-grammatical errors (Bonilla López et al., 2018). The design is rigorous in its random assignment and delayed posttest, but the self-report measure limits what can be claimed about processing effort.

In a survey of 70 students in a university ESL program in the southwestern United States, students favoured direct correction with metalinguistic explanations (215/447, 48.10%), followed by direct correction alone (111/447, 24.83%) (Liu and Wu, 2019). Their descriptive, non-randomised questionnaire design limits inference, and the authors themselves note the data are necessarily descriptive (Liu and Wu, 2019).
